heard: A spacecraft once found strange, linear scars carved into a deep space rock. In 1991, NASA's Galileo spacecraft approached the asteroid 951 Gaspra while traveling toward Jupiter. Since its discovery in 1916, astronomers saw Gaspra as nothing more than a tiny point of light. Galileo closed the gap, snapping 57 images from as close as 3,300 miles away. The resolution revealed details just 54 meters wide, showing a jagged world lacking large impact craters. But the biggest shock was the linear grooves, which had previously only been seen on the Martian moon Phobos. These fractures suggest Gaspara was born from the violent, catastrophic breakup of a much larger parent asteroid. It was the first time humanity saw the scars carved into a deep space rock.
